newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore wants more bids for telecoms licences.
newsitem.headline: Singapore wants more bids for telecoms licences.

text.p: Singapore Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan said on Wednesday he hoped many more companies would express interest in bidding for a licence to operate basic telecommunications services in the city-state.
Mah told reporters it was too early to say how many additional licences would be issued and said it depended on the quality of the bids received.
Singapore has said it will issue one or two new licences to operate telephones and other basic telecoms services in its domestic market from April 2000.

"I am happy with the quality of the players that have publicly indicated their interest in the basic telecoms licence," Mah said. "They are players which, I am sure would not have any trouble putting up a very good tender proposal.
"However, I welcome many more players, many more interested parties to come forward with their statements of intent."
The Singapore telephone market is currently operated as a monopoly by state-owned Singapore Telecommunications Ltd .
So far at least three consortiums have indicated serious interest in bidding for a Singapore licence.
These include a number of foreign companies such as British Telecommunications Plc and Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
Asked if the government might change its mind on the number of basic telecommunications licences and issue more than two new licences, Mah replied: "No."
Earlier, he announced Singapore would further liberalise its cellular mobile telephone services market and call for tenders later this year to award up to two more licenses from year 2000.
